subject: Deployment mode decision: MAP milestones and cutover risk register
messages:
From: Emily Wang <emily@cardioai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cardioai.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP and deployment questions

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The execs liked Redwood's latency numbers, but we need to lock the deployment mode and target region in our MAP before our procurement kickoff on Nov 20.

Key asks from our side:
- Preferred path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and what triggers each path in the MAP.
- A short cutover/rollback plan if we start on Hosted and need to move to Dedicated.
- Any gating items that would push us to choose Private (on‑prem/VPC) e.g., data residency, HSM requirements.

We have two products: non-PHI triage (can be multi-region US) and PHI-sensitive claims processing (requires stricter controls). We want a staged approach but need milestone dates and who owns each item so procurement can slot payments.

Can you send a draft MAP with checkpoints and escalation paths? Also include SLA expectations per mode and any evidence we can attach to our security review.

Cheers,
Emily
Emily Wang
Head of Platform Operations
CardioAI

[Attachment: initial-reqs-cardioai.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Wang <emily@cardioai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP and deployment questions

Emily — thanks, and great context. Draft MAP attached (MAP_CardioAI_v2.xlsx). High level proposal:

1) Phase 1 (Discovery → PoC → Pilot) [Target: Nov 20 → Dec 18]
   - Mode: Hosted (single-US region, multi-az) for rapid time-to-value.
   - Milestones: PoC (week 2), Pilot (week 6), Production readiness checklist (week 8).

2) Phase 2 (Regulated Workload Separation) [Target: Jan 2027]
   - Mode options: Dedicated reserved capacity for PHI workflows; Hosted for non-PHI.
   - Trigger to move to Dedicated: signed contract with 99.95% latency SLO + reserved capacity commit.

3) Phase 3 (Optional Private)
   - Mode: Private (VPC or on‑prem) for customers requiring customer‑managed networking, HSM/KMS in-custody, or strict data residency.
   - Trigger: legal/regulatory clause or procurement requiring on‑prem.

Rollback/cutover notes (short):
- If we begin on Hosted and need to move to Dedicated: schedule a dedicated provisioning window (2–4 weeks) with data sync using our KV export/import and prefix cache warmers. We recommend a canary cutover for 10% traffic for 48h then gradual 25/50/100.
- Rollback plan: fail back to Hosted by re-routing traffic and using snapshot reattach; retain inbound queue to avoid loss. Estimated outage window for cutover: 15–45 minutes for connection switch; warmup extension depends on model cache state.

I've included an SLA summary PDF and a SOC2 impact matrix we typically share with procurement. See attachments.

Next steps: If this aligns, we can convert the MAP into a mutual action plan link (HubSpot + sign‑off milestones) and propose a committed Dedicated estimate for your PHI lane.

- Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: MAP_CardioAI_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet); Attachment: Redwood-Hosting-SLA-summary.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Emily Wang <emily@cardioai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP and deployment questions

Emily / team — adding a couple of technical clarifications from an infra perspective:

- Dedicated provisioning lead time: depending on instance class and region, reserved pool provisioning is typically 7–21 calendar days after contract signature for standard configs; custom hardware (HSM/air‑gapped) will be longer.
- Data residency: Private deployment is the only guaranteed way to keep all inference artifacts inside your VPC/on‑prem. For Hosted/Dedicated we offer strong network controls and optional regional tenancy but not a physical-only guarantee.
- QA gating: if your security team requires penetration testing on the inference runtime, we recommend scheduling that during Pilot and before production rollout to avoid delaying cutover.

I've attached a SOC2 impact matrix that maps CardioAI asks to evidence we can provide and where Dedicated vs Private differ.

Two asks for the MAP spreadsheet before we finalize:
1) Add owner column for each milestone (Redwood PM, CardioAI Eng, Legal).
2) Add acceptance criteria for the PHI lane (encryption-at-rest with customer KMS, audit log retention 13 months, SOC2 evidence set).

On the rollback item — note that moving from Dedicated back to Hosted is uncommon but supported; timeline is mainly driven by capacity deprovisioning and rehydration of caches. We'll call out estimated costs for dual-running both modes in the MAP.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: SOC2-Impact-Matrix.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Wang <emily@cardioai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP and deployment questions

Emily — thanks for the clarifications and for surfacing PHI requirements. Per our internal sync, here's an action-oriented mutual action plan summary and decision capture for procurement: 

Summary decision (as of 2026-11-16):
- Immediate: Proceed with Hosted (single-US region) for non-PHI triage workloads.
- Commit intent: Reserve Dedicated capacity for PHI claims lane; signature on a Dedicated commitment (term: 12 months) triggers provisioning.
- Private: remains on the table if CardioAI legal signs an on‑prem/VPC clause or requests HSM-in-custody.

Mutual action milestones (owners in parentheses):
- 2026-11-20: Procurement kickoff (CardioAI Legal).
- 2026-11-27: PoC results and perf signoff (CardioAI Eng / Redwood Solutions).
- 2026-12-18: Pilot complete, QA & PT scheduled (CardioAI QA / Redwood Infra).
- 2027-01-10: Decision to commit to Dedicated (CardioAI Exec / Redwood Sales).
- 2027-01-24: Dedicated provisioning window begins (Redwood Infra).

Cutover & rollback criteria (short):
- Canary window: 48h at 10% traffic, success = error rate < 0.5% and latency within agreed SLO.
- If canary fails: rollback to Hosted routing and open an incident with 3-day remediation SLA.

Costs & dual-run note: we include estimated dual-run costs as a 10–20% uplift during the transition phase; we'll add exact numbers to the MAP spreadsheet for procurement to review.

Attachments and links for procurement pack: MAP_CardioAI_v2.xlsx; SOC2-Impact-Matrix.pdf; Redwood-Hosting-SLA-summary.pdf; HubSpot deal link; DocuSign for Dedicated commitment.

If this reflects CardioAI's expectations, we'll publish the MAP to the HubSpot deal and create a DocuSign envelope for the Dedicated term sheet. Please reply with any changes by EOD Nov 18 so procurement can meet the target kickoff.

Best,
Sean
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
